writeup.1: A towel is the cheapest thing hanging off a bag, which is why eighteen brands treat that rectangle of terry cotton as the place to put a whole idea. The category reads better up close than it does from the cart path.
writeup.2: The best of them do something a towel has no obligation to do. Agronomy Workshop prints theirs to look like a crumpled paper bag. Seamus had Pendleton weave the Wyeth Trail as a jacquard rather than printing a picture of one. Mogshade and Parmore put blackletter type on cream and shot it against a wall covered in graffiti.
writeup.3: Prices run $29 to $58, with four brands charging in kronor, pounds and Australian dollars instead. Matchstick holds the bottom of that range and Malbon the top. Several of these are sold out, which counts for less on a towel than it would on a shoe, because they are repeat items and the brands restock them.
